title: GRAPHO-ANALYTICAL ANALYSIS OF THE CHARACTERISTICS OF OBLIQUE CUTTING OF STOCHASTIC SOIL STRUCTURE BY THE FLEXIBLE WIRE OF A SOIL-DEEPENING TOOL
abstractText: The design features of most modern tillage implements determine a characteristic aspect of their operating processes associated with the oblique-angle cutting regime applied to the heterogeneous and stochastic structure of the soil. Therefore, a detailed study of soil deformation and failure under oblique cutting conditions is important for substantiating and optimizing the structural and operational parameters of innovative tillage machinery at the stages of development, design and further practical application. The paper presents the results of a graphical-analytical investigation of the oblique cutting characteristics of a “flexible wire” subsoiler intended for loosening over-compacted sub-arable soil layers and eliminating the negative effects of a plow pan. Based on the obtained research results, the structural layout of the proposed subsoiler was substantiated. Its design incorporates a double-acting mechanical damper installed within the “flexible string” circuit. The application of this element makes it possible to significantly reduce the draft resistance of the subsoiler by promoting soil failure mainly through a system of longitudinal and transverse shear cracks propagating toward the open surface of the soil half-space. This operating principle reduces unnecessary compaction and improves the energy efficiency of deep soil loosening. The installation of the mechanical damper induces controlled self-excited oscillations of the flexible working element, thereby ensuring stable oblique cutting along the entire contour of the “flexible string”, regardless of local changes in its curvature during interaction with the soil. It was established that the use of an 8 mm gauge G80 grade short-link load chain manufactured in accordance with ASTM A391 as the flexible subsoiler string provides an average transverse dimension of approximately 20 mm. Furthermore, a tillage unit consisting of a PLN-5-35 plow combined with the developed flexible subsoiler, designed for loosening a sub-plow layer with a plow-pan thickness of 100 mm, ensures an operating depth of h = 0.35–0.40 m. The obtained results can be used to improve the design of deep-loosening implements, reduce draft force and energy consumption, and increase the efficiency of till.

title: SIEM Logs as Digital Evidence: Reliability, Integrity, and Challenges in Cybercrime Investigations
abstractText: Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) systems are widely used to collect, correlate, and analyse logs for cybersecurity monitoring and incident response. However, the growing reliance on SIEM data during digital forensic and cybercrime investigations raises important questions about whether such logs can be treated as reliable digital evidence. This paper examines the factors that influence the evidential value of SIEM logs through a conceptual research design supported by a structured integrative review of literature from cybersecurity, digital forensics, log management, incident response, and digital evidence preservation. The analysis develops four propositions relating to source-log quality, preservation and chain of custody, transparency of SIEM processing, and the effects of timestamp inconsistencies, weak access controls, incomplete logging, and deliberate manipulation. The findings show that SIEM evidential reliability depends on the entire logging lifecycle and not just on the kind of SIEM platform used. High-quality source logs, strong integrity controls, clear chain of custody procedures, and transparent correlation and normalisation processes strengthen evidential value, while incomplete records, weak preservation practices, and manipulation reduce confidence in forensic conclusions. The paper argues that SIEM platforms should be treated as part of a wider digital evidence ecosystem. Organisations should therefore incorporate forensic requirements into logging, preservation, and security-monitoring practices before incidents occur. Future empirical research should test the proposed relationships across different SIEM platforms and investigative environments.

Taxifolin alleviates podocyte injury and macrophage chemotaxis associated with diabetic nephropathy by directly targeting RBP1 identified via multi-omics and machine learning
abstractText: Aims Podocyte injury contributes to diabetic nephropathy (DN) progression. This study aimed to screen and validate the key functional proteins related to podocyte injury in DN, and to explore the protective effect of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine Linggui Zhugan (LGZG) formula against DN. Methods Proteomics, weighted gene co-expression network analysis, machine learning, and repeated out-of-fold exact SHapley Additive exPlanations (TreeSHAP) analysis were integrated to screen the top 15 core differentially expressed proteins in kidney tissues of DN patients. Single-cell transcriptomics and cell-cell communication analysis were further used to identify the podocyte protein retinol-binding protein 1 (RBP1). In vitro , a palmitic acid (PA)-induced podocyte injury model and gene knockdown experiments were performed to verify the regulatory function of RBP1. Molecular docking and microscale thermophoresis (MST) were applied to screen and confirm the binding interaction between bioactive ingredients of LGZG formula and RBP1. The renoprotective effect of taxifolin was further evaluated in this cell model. Results Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identified RBP1 as a key pathogenic molecule in DN patients. In vitro , PA stimulation increased RBP1 protein expression in podocyte injury, with the downregulation of podocyte-specific slit diaphragm proteins nephrin and synaptopodin, and the upregulation of pro-inflammatory mediators including C-C motif chemokine ligand 2 ( CCL2 ), interleukin-6 ( IL-6 ), and tumor necrosis factor-α ( TNF-α ), as well as enhanced macrophage chemotaxis. Notably, RBP1 knockdown reversed these PA-induced alterations to alleviate podocyte injury. Taxifolin from LGZG formula directly bound RBP1, as confirmed by molecular docking and MST. Furthermore, taxifolin was found to bind to RBP1. And then it suppressed nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway, reduced CCL2 , IL-6 and TNF-α mRNA expression, inhibited macrophage chemotaxis, and upregulated nephrin and synaptopodin expression, thereby ameliorating PA-induced podocyte injury. Conclusion This study identified RBP1 as a novel driver of podocyte injury and macrophage chemotaxis associated with DN via multi-omics and machine learning. Taxifolin, a bioactive compound from the LGZG formula, directly bound to RBP1 and alleviated podocyte injury. These findings highlight RBP1 as a promising therapeutic target and support the potential of taxifolin as a targeted intervention for DN progression.

title: Integrating temperature and CO2-concentration impact on crops into an input–output framework
abstractText: Abstract Environmental Input–Output Analysis (IOA) incorporates feedbacks in coupled economic-environmental systems, driven by an exogenous demand and fixed input–output coefficients with a linearity assumption. For some environmental problems, or over longer time periods, the IO coefficients and exogenous drivers may change. Here, we introduce a climate-feedback into an IO system via the crop sector to illustrate the potential couplings between climate change and material and economic flows. We use existing climate impact ensembles to calibrate climate feedback parameters for crop productivity and implement them in an expanded IO system. We generally find that the same exogenous demand can be met with lower output due to yield improvements, driven by the beneficial effect of CO 2 fertilization which generally dominates the modelled temperature effect on yield, essentially indicating a reduction in land-use intensity driven by CO2 fertilization. However, the temperature effect, which is positive or negative dependent on region, may be underestimated because of the inability of existing process-based models to simulate climate-related agricultural impacts. The overall changes in yield, when exogenous demand is held fixed and annual CO 2 emissions are used as feedback, are of the order of 0.2% when normalized with the regional crop outputs and much smaller when normalized with total output. While the impact of a single year’s emissions is small, climate change is a cumulative problem and becomes significant over decades. Over these time periods, economic structure and demand would be expected to change in response to the climate impacts, requiring a dynamic modelling framework.

title: The Effect of Salinity Variation on the Blood Profile and Physiological Adaptation of Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus)
abstractText: Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) is a major freshwater aquaculture species with potential for culture in brackish environments, but increasing salinity may impose osmotic stress and alter physiological performance. This study evaluated the effects of salinity on the blood profile, survival, and physiological adaptation of Nile tilapia. A completely randomized design was used with five salinity treatments (0, 5, 10, 15, and 20 ppt), each with three replicates. Hematocrit, hemoglobin concentration, erythrocyte count, leukocyte count, blood glucose concentration, survival rate, and water quality were assessed. Increasing salinity significantly affected the hematological and physiological responses of Nile tilapia. Erythrocyte counts and hemoglobin concentrations decreased as salinity increased, whereas leukocyte counts, hematocrit values, and blood glucose concentrations increased. Survival tended to decline with increasing salinity, with the lowest value (73.33%) recorded at 20 ppt. These responses indicate increasing osmoregulatory and metabolic stress at higher salinity levels. Under the conditions tested, salinity levels of ≤10 ppt provided a more favorable range for maintaining physiological stability and survival of Nile tilapia.

title: Digital Marketing, Competitive Advantage, and Madrasah Choice: Mediating Role of Stoic Rationality
abstractText: Purpose: This study examines the role of Stoic rationality in prospective students’ school selection decisions and its mediating effects on the relationships between digital marketing, competitive advantage, and school selection decisions. Research Method: An explanatory quantitative approach was employed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. Data were collected through purposive sampling from 96 prospective students of MA Ma’arif 7 Sunan Drajat, Lamongan Regency. Results and Discussion: Digital marketing significantly enhances Stoic rationality but has no significant direct effect on school selection decisions. Competitive advantage positively influences both Stoic rationality and school selection decisions. Stoic rationality significantly influences school selection decisions, fully mediating the effect of digital marketing and partially mediating the effect of competitive advantage. Implications: The findings highlight rational evaluation as a mechanism linking institutional strategies to educational choices. Islamic schools should strengthen competitive differentiation and develop digital marketing that supports informed decisions. The single-institution setting and limited sample constrain generalizability. Originality: This study integrates Stoic rationality into educational choice research, demonstrating that digital marketing influences school selection indirectly through rational evaluation rather than directly.

title: EDUKASI DAGUSIBU TERINTEGRASI BUD BAGI KARANG TARUNA DUSUN JOMBOR DESA SUMBEREJO
abstractText: Penggunaan obat yang tidak rasional masih menjadi masalah kesehatan utama, terutama pada kelompok remaja dan dewasa muda yang melakukan swamedikasi tanpa pengetahuan teknis yang memadai. Limbah obat yang dibuang sembarangan juga berpotensi mencemari lingkungan. Program DAGUSIBU (Dapatkan, Gunakan, Simpan, Buang) yang diinisiasi oleh Ikatan Apoteker Indonesia hadir sebagai upaya meningkatkan pengetahuan masyarakat dalam mengelola obat secara rasional. Namun, pemahaman tentang DAGUSIBU tidak lengkap tanpa pengetahuan tentang BUD (Beyond Use Date), yaitu batas waktu penggunaan obat setelah kemasan dibuka. BUD merupakan materi penting yang memperkuat pilar "Buang" pada DAGUSIBU. Kegiatan pengabdian ini bertujuan meningkatkan pengetahuan karang taruna di Dusun Jombor, Desa Sumberejo, Klaten, mengenai DAGUSIBU yang terintegrasi dengan BUD. Kegiatan dilaksanakan di Dusun Jombor dengan 27 peserta. Metode yang digunakan adalah edukasi interaktif dengan ceramah, diskusi, dan tanya jawab, didukung leaflet dan video. Evaluasi dilakukan melalui kuesioner post-test. Hasil menunjukkan rata-rata tingkat pengetahuan BUD sebesar 97,8% (kategori baik), dan DAGUSIBU sebesar 88,88% (kategori baik). Persentase jawaban benar tertinggi untuk BUD adalah tentang sirup kering (92,6%), sedangkan terendah tentang kapsul dan tablet yang tahan dalam kondisi lembab (81,4%). Untuk DAGUSIBU, tertinggi tentang aturan pakai obat (100%), terendah tentang menghabiskan antibiotik (81,48%). Dapat disimpulkan bahwa edukasi terintegrasi ini efektif meningkatkan pengetahuan peserta. Diperlukan edukasi lanjutan untuk mengoreksi miskonsepsi, terutama terkait penggunaan antibiotik dan penyimpanan obat.

STUDY OF THE DYNAMIC CHARACTERISTICS OF A MULTIFUNCTIONAL ROTARY WORKING UNIT
abstractText: A mathematical model of the dynamics of a multifunctional rotary working unit was developed, and the influence of its structural and kinematic parameters on the critical shaft rotation speed and the amplitude-frequency characteristics was investigated. The working unit is considered as a complex mechanical system comprising an elastic shaft with discretely placed concentrated masses, as well as hinge-mounted flail hammers. The relevance of the study lies in establishing the characteristic rotation frequency zones under the condition of ensuring resonance-free operation of the rotor. To construct the dynamic model, an energy-based approach and the Lagrange equations of the second kind were used. The model accounts for the energy of the shaft, the discretely placed masses, and the variable position of the flail hammers, as well as energy losses due to damping and the destruction of plant mass. As a result of the simulation, the equation of motion of the rotor was obtained, on the basis of which an expression was derived for determining the critical shaft rotation speed and the amplitude-frequency characteristic of the system. A numerical experiment was conducted for an experimental rotor sample, which established that at an effective mass of 50.087 kg and a radial shaft stiffness of N/m, the critical rotation speed is 220.078 rad/s. The influences of effective mass, radial shaft stiffness, viscous damping coefficient, and imbalance magnitude on the position of the resonance zone and the oscillation amplitude were substantiated. It was established that an increase in the rotor's effective mass reduces the critical rotation speed, while an increase in shaft stiffness contributes to its growth. It is shown that an increase in damping significantly reduces the maximum oscillation amplitude in the resonance zone, whereas an increase in imbalance causes a proportional increase in vibrational loads. Based on the simulation results, it was established that the working range of the rotor rotation frequency of 1200-1300 rpm lies in the pre-resonance zone and is characterized by insignificant oscillation amplitudes. The obtained value of the safety factor with respect to the critical frequency is 1.617, which indicates a sufficient distance of the operating mode from the resonance region.

Content Convergence and Audience Engagement on Platform X: A Study of the @RadioElshinta Account
abstractText: Background: Digital platforms enable radio stations to distribute information beyond conventional broadcasts and provide observable indicators of audience response. Understanding how a news radio account organizes its content on social media can help describe its digital communication practices. Objective: This study describes the content presented by Radio Elshinta through its @RadioElshinta account on Platform X and maps observable audience responses across content categories. Methods: A descriptive quantitative approach using social media content analysis was applied to all 2,175 posts recorded from 1 April to 31 May 2026. Each post was assigned to one primary content category. Presentation formats, likes, reposts, replies, and views were documented, and the data were summarized using counts, percentages, and descriptive comparisons. Results: The findings show that 2,175 posts were published during the observation period, with real-time traffic updates representing the largest content category with 790 posts (36.32%), followed by talk-show summaries with 547 posts (25.15%) and national news and politics with 383 posts (17.61%). Content was presented through various formats, including text, images, videos, audio clips, and links. Audience engagement varied across content categories, with category-specific engagement rates ranging from 0.16% to 0.58%, while the overall average engagement rate ranged from 0.18% to 0.35%. Conclusion: The findings indicate that the @RadioElshinta account functioned as a digital distribution channel that presented diverse information formats and content categories during the observation period. The observed differences in engagement across content categories provide a descriptive basis for understanding audience responses to radio-related content distributed through Platform X.

title: Patient-specific hemodynamic evaluation of fenestrated physician-modified endografts in complex abdominal aortic aneurysms
abstractText: Purpose Physician-modified endografts (PMEGs) are increasingly used for complex abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), but the patient-specific flow consequences of the geometric reconstruction are not well quantified. This study evaluated PMEG-associated changes in hemodynamic and wall-mechanical surrogate markers. Materials and Methods Eight patients were retrospectively analyzed. Pre- and post-PMEG geometries were reconstructed from computed tomography angiography and simulated with pulsatile computational fluid dynamics under matched inlet and outlet conditions. Time-averaged wall shear stress relative residence time and endothelial cell activation potential were quantified; one representative case underwent fluid-structure interaction analysis. Results Mean velocity increased from approximately 0.8–1.5 m/s ( P = 0.0021), pressure drop decreased ( P = 0.0183), low-shear regions became less extensive, and RRT and ECAP decreased significantly (both P < 0.05). FSI showed lower computed wall deformation after repair. At 1 year, all branch stents remained patent, with no endoleak or reported adverse event. Conclusion Together with prior paired PMEG simulations, these findings support a favorable hemodynamic and wall-mechanical effect of PMEG in complex anatomy unsuitable for conventional infrarenal EVAR and suggest a less stasis-prone postoperative environment. Larger controlled cohorts remain necessary to determine whether these surrogate changes translate into fewer clinical thrombotic or rupture events. The observed changes arise from PMEG-induced geometric remodeling, which modifies local flow acceleration, separation, near-wall shear, and pressure-loss characteristics.

Temporal RNA-seq analysis reveals previously uncharacterized B cell infiltration during late chronic cerebral toxoplasmosis
abstractText: Chronic toxoplasmosis begins when tachyzoites cross the blood–brain barrier and enter the Central Nervous System (CNS). There, they differentiate into bradyzoites, which persist in tissue cysts. Here, we investigate changes in host gene expression in the mouse brain by RNA sequencing at different time points during chronic toxoplasmosis. We show a conserved gene expression pattern caused by the infection, primarily associated with cytotoxic immune responses against the parasite and neuronal degeneration, regardless of the time point. Surprisingly, we observed that genes associated with B cell function continuously increased over time, whilst cytotoxic responses decreased. Immunoglobulin gene expression and IgA staining showed that B cells were absent from healthy brains. Following infection, they accumulated near penetrating vessels and infiltrated the brain parenchyma. Additionally, these plasma cells produced T. gondii -specific IgA. Our results show a previously unrecognized expansion of brain B cells in late chronic toxoplasmosis.

title: Socioeconomic costs and health-related quality of life associated with oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy
abstractText: Background Oculopharyngeal muscular dystrophy (OPMD) is a progressive genetic neuromuscular disease. OPMD substantially impacts quality of life by limiting swallowing, decreasing mobility and can cause death by choking. We conducted this study to quantify the burden of OPMD from the patient perspective. These data are needed to inform cost-effectiveness studies for treatments in development and to inform public policy. Methods As part of the national Burden of Inherited and Inflammatory Neuromuscular Disease study survey, Canadians with OPMD were asked about the impact of OPMD on their health-related quality of life (Health Utilities Index Mark 3; HUI3), employment status, household finances, productivity (Work Productivity and Activity Impairment questionnaire), and out-of-pocket costs for assistive equipment and healthcare to help manage OPMD. Sociodemographic and epidemiological data were used to extrapolate participant responses into an estimate of the total patient-borne cost of OPMD for Canada. Results Health-related quality of life was low in OPMD ( n = 139, mean age 66 ± 10 years, 52% female) with HUI3 scores of 0.398 ± 0.323, compared to 0.826 for the normative population. Low HUI3 scores were associated with higher costs for assistive equipment and greater financial hardship. 29% of respondents with OPMD were in paid employment compared to 41% in the normative population. Impairments in total work productivity and non-work activity were 32 ± 27% and 61 ± 29%, respectively. Paid employment was associated with greater access to private insurance (odds ratio 4.2) which was in turn positively associated with the likelihood of visiting allied healthcare providers (odds ratio 2.5). The total patient-borne cost of OPMD for Canada was estimated to be $78.4 million (2026 Canadian dollars). Indirect costs accounted for 84% of the total; 53% for non-work activity impairment, 18% for loss of earning capacity, 12% for presenteeism and 2% for absenteeism. Direct costs comprised 16% of the total; 7% for healthcare visits and 9% for assistive equipment. Discussion OPMD imposes substantial direct and indirect economic burden, primarily due to impact on work and productivity and less on equipment or health professional costs. The high indirect costs of OPMD should be a consideration in economic evaluations and future health policy decisions for emerging therapeutic interventions.

title: Effect of a potassium-competitive acid blocker on the gut microbiota in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention: a randomized pilot study
abstractText: Background and aim Proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) are routinely used in patients undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to prevent gastrointestinal bleeding associated with dual-antiplatelet therapy (DAPT). However, long-term PPI use has been linked to gut microbiota dysbiosis. Tegoprazan, a potassium-competitive acid blocker (P-CAB), may exert distinct effects on the gut microbiome. This study compared the longitudinal effects of tegoprazan and pantoprazole on gut microbiota composition in patients with angina undergoing PCI. Methods This prospective, randomized, controlled pilot study randomized 38 patients 1:1:1 to tegoprazan 50 mg once daily, pantoprazole 40 mg once daily, or no acid-suppressive therapy for 24 weeks. Five participants did not provide baseline fecal samples, and nine discontinued participation before week 24. Thus, 24 participants with paired baseline and week-24 fecal samples were included in the final analysis. Fecal samples were analyzed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing. Results No drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding occurred in any group. Observed amplicon sequence variant (ASV) richness was significantly higher at week 24 than at baseline in the overall cohort (p = 0.003) and P-CAB group (p = 0.016), whereas the Shannon index showed no significant changes. Paired PERMANOVA with permutations restricted by patient ID revealed significant differences in Bray–Curtis beta diversity between baseline and week 24 in the P-CAB group (R² = 0.070, p = 0.031) and PPI group (R² = 0.059, p = 0.008), but not in the no acid-suppressive therapy group (R² = 0.021, p = 0.691). In the formal cross-arm analysis, the treatment group-by-visit interaction was not significant for Bray–Curtis beta diversity (R² = 0.021, pseudo-F = 0.505, p = 0.270). Although nominal within-arm taxonomic changes were observed, no treatment group-by-visit interaction survived Benjamini–Hochberg correction in ANCOM-BC2. Conclusion Tegoprazan was well tolerated, with no drug-related adverse events or gastrointestinal bleeding during the 24-week follow-up. Both acid-suppressive treatment groups showed modest longitudinal microbiome changes. The taxon-level findings were exploratory and hypothesis-generating and should not be interpreted as definitive evidence of treatment-specific differential effects. Larger, adequately powered studies are required to confirm these observations.

title: Living With Known Unknowns: Prognostic Uncertainty in Congenital Cytomegalovirus Following Diagnosis
abstractText: OBJECTIVE To examine how parents experience and navigate prognostic uncertainty following a diagnosis of congenital cytomegalovirus (cCMV) and identify implications for clinical communication and newborn screening. METHODS We conducted in-depth qualitative interviews with 41 birth parents of children with cCMV. Interviews explored diagnosis, communication with health care practitioners, health care navigation, and perceptions of child development. Transcripts were analyzed using inductive reflexive thematic analysis. RESULTS Prognostic uncertainty emerged as a central and enduring feature of parents’ experiences. Five themes characterized how families navigated uncertainty: (1) families live with the burden of an unpredictable future, (2) families struggle to make meaning from incomplete and inconsistent information, (3) families become drivers of the diagnostic journey to gain clarity and control, (4) knowledge provides families direction even when certainty is impossible, and (5) families value early diagnosis because it makes uncertainty more manageable. Uncertainty contributed to anxiety, information seeking, and ongoing monitoring. However, parents consistently valued early diagnosis because it provided direction, facilitated treatment and developmental surveillance, supported access to intervention, and informed decision-making. Rather than eliminating uncertainty, diagnosis transformed an unpredictable future into possibilities on which families could monitor and act. CONCLUSIONS Prognostic uncertainty is an inherent and longitudinal feature of cCMV and should be acknowledged in counseling following the diagnosis. Despite persistent uncertainty, parents valued early identification because it provided direction and opportunities for surveillance and intervention. As cCMV screening expands, family-centered communication, anticipatory guidance, care coordination, and longitudinal support can help families navigate uncertainty over time.

Numerical analysis of mechanical anchors in hybrid bonded FRP strengthening system
abstractText: Abstract To address the issues of unreasonable torque control and unclear failure modes in concrete anchorage systems with chemical anchors in hybrid bonded Fiber-Reinforced Polymer (FRP) strengthening system, this study focuses on the numerical simulation analysis of bolt-concrete anchorage systems. The mechanical characteristics and concrete failure modes under different anchorage depths, load levels and torque limits are emphatically investigated. Using the finite element numerical simulation method, a three-dimensional model of the bolt-concrete anchorage system is established, in which concrete is modelled with 8-node hexahedral solid elements and bolts with 6-node pentahedral solid elements. A full-bond interface assumption with common nodes is adopted between the two components. Multiple groups of numerical simulations are carried out by varying the parameters of anchorage depth and tightening torque, and the bolt stress, concrete crack propagation and failure patterns are analyzed. The results show that anchorage depth is the dominant factor controlling the ultimate bearing capacity of the anchorage system, and different anchorage depths correspond to different stress attenuation paths. At a medium embedment depth of 50 mm, a mixed failure mode consisting of upper concrete cone failure and lower interfacial bond failure is observed. Based on the simulation results, the recommended limit for bolt tightening torque is determined to be 13 N·m, which can effectively prevent damage to the concrete substrate caused by excessive pre-tightening force. The findings can provide a theoretical reference for the engineering design and torque control of concrete anchorage systems with chemical anchors.

title: Reading in healthy aging: how attentional components drive age-related changes
abstractText: Abstract Background Reading represents a cognitively engaging activity that supports the maintenance of cognitive functioning in older adults. Even though it has been extensively documented that reading is influenced by the aging process itself, the high-level cognitive mechanisms behind this decline remain poorly understood. This study aimed at examining the role of cognitive functions and particularly of the selective visuo-spatial attention in the age-related changes in reading. Method One hundred-twenty neurologically healthy older adults (age range 60–88; mean age: 70.64 ± 5.48) underwent a neuropsychological assessment measuring reading abilities, global cognitive functioning, attention, and visual skills. Results Results revealed that general cognitive components (i.e., inhibition, working memory and speed processing), as assessed by the simple reaction times task, Stroop test and Symbol Digit Modalities Test, significantly mediated the relationship between age and reading performance. Visuo-spatial attention specifically appeared to moderate this relationship: individuals with greater decline in visual search tasks showed an amplified impact of age on reading abilities. Conclusion These findings highlight that reading is a multifaceted cognitive process, whose age-related decline reflects the interplay of several general and specific cognitive factors. The moderating role of visuo-spatial attention underscores the importance of accounting for individual variability in healthy aging.

title: Perceived stress, dental environmental stress, and academic performance among dental students: a cross-sectional study
abstractText: Objectives This study investigated perceived stress and dental environmental stress among dental students, their relationships with academic performance, and the potential association of participation in the Integrative Mind-Body Wellness Initiative (IMBWI) with students’ well-being and academic outcomes. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted among dental students at the UCLA School of Dentistry. Participants completed the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10) and the Dental Environment Stress (DES) questionnaire, along with self-reported demographic and academic measures, including academic performance. Regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with stress outcomes and academic performance. Spearman's correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between stress scores and academic performance, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Results Mean (SD) PSS and DES scores were 21.64 (6.74) and 58.03 (15.53), respectively, indicating moderate stress levels. Academic- and personal-related stressors represented the highest-scoring DES domains. PSS and DES scores demonstrated a moderate positive correlation ( ρ = 0.65, p = 0.001). Academic ranking showed weak, non-significant negative correlations with both PSS ( ρ = −0.20, p = 0.08) and DES scores ( ρ = −0.09, p = 0.43). Students reporting ≥10 weekly hours of self-care activities had significantly lower odds of high environmental stress (OR = 0.19, 95% CI: 0.05–0.62, p = 0.009). Greater study time outside scheduled academic activities was similarly associated with lower odds of high environmental stress (OR = 0.20, 95% CI: 0.05–0.67, p = 0.013). Participation in the IMBWI demonstrated a non-significant trend toward lower stress levels. Conclusions Dental students demonstrated moderate levels of perceived and environmental stress. Greater engagement in self-care activities and independent study time was associated with lower environmental stress levels. These findings support the importance of promoting student well-being and supportive learning environments within dental education.

title: From shared reading to self-narration: a developmental pathway for reading-based psychological support
abstractText: Reading-based psychological support is usually studied as clinical bibliotherapy, shared reading, or literacy-related intervention, and these strands are rarely followed across childhood, adolescence, and emerging adulthood. This perspective asks whether shared reading can become a source of self-narration. In childhood, reading with a responsive adult may support emotional language and meaning-making. During adolescence, some narrative resources may be selectively taken up and revised. In emerging adulthood, they may be used to organize transitions, commitments, and possible futures into an evolving life story. The account presents this as a developmental hypothesis rather than as evidence that childhood reading causes later narrative identity. Reading is treated as a complement to mental-health treatment, not as a substitute. The result is a set of empirical questions about mediation, developmental timing, relational quality, and contextual confounding.

title: Enabling monocular collision avoidance in a smart hangar
abstractText: Abstract Hangar-based maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) operations expose aircraft to close-proximity interactions with ground support equipment (GSE), where operator errors can cause structural damage and disruption. This study presents a monocular vision framework for collision-risk monitoring in a smart hangar, coupling instance segmentation, domain-adapted monocular depth inference and deterministic clearance reasoning. A paired dataset comprises synthetic top-down hangar renderings with pixel-aligned red-green-blue (RGB)-depth supervision and a matched miniature testbed containing scaled aircraft/GSE models and 3D-printed calibration objects, imaged by custom-mounted RGB cameras. The dual-head pipeline comprises YOLOv8-seg for six-class instance masks and DepthAnything-V2 for metric depth under the trained model convention. On the scene-disjoint synthetic test split, the custom-trained depth model achieves 0.135 m MAE, compared with 8.385m for pretrained weights, without materially increasing depth-inference time. WIthout dense RBG-camera depth ground truth, testbed-image transfer is reported as an ordinal/structural calibration-object proxy: relative step ordering is often preserved, whereas inter-step metric spacing is compressed and deemed inadequate for direct clearance-threshold decisions. Custom YOLOv8-seg variants achieve mean Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.88–0.92 across synthetic and testbed splits, while the off-the-shelf baseline yields near-zero overlap in transfer tests. Collision inference is evaluated on deterministic 30-image samples per synthetic/testbed scenario, combining depth-derived height envelopes and boundary-only ground-plane distances to produce clear/warning/alert states and overlays. Median no-render compute latency is 0.736–1.037 s; profiling identifies post-processing, particularly GSE clustering and geometry construction, as the dominant runtime component. The study provides an auditable perception-to-geometry pipeline and highlights the need for uncertainty-aware threshold calibration before deployment.

title: Beyond binary: a novel anatomical-geographical-biological framework for perineural invasion risk stratification in oral squamous cell carcinoma – a proof-of-concept study
abstractText: Background Perineural invasion (PNI) is an adverse pathological feature in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and an indication for adjuvant radiotherapy but is conventionally reported as a binary variable. The prognostic relevance of its quantitative morphological features remains incompletely defined. Materials and methods In this single-centre retrospective cohort, 101 consecutive patients with pathologically node-negative OSCC treated by curative-intent resection (January 2023 – March 2024) were analysed. Six block-level morphological PNI parameters were assessed on digitised H&E whole-slide images by two pathologists: largest involved nerve diameter (P1), maximum nerves involved (P2), pattern of invasion (P3; intratumoural, extratumoural or both), maximum circumferential extent (P4), nerves with mitotic figures (P5), and minimum distance from the tumour front to the nearest uninvolved nerve (P6). Interobserver reproducibility was evaluated for all five PNI parameters. Cutpoints were derived by maximally selected rank statistics. Univariate and bivariable Cox regression, bootstrap stability, and a composite 0–6 score were evaluated against disease-free survival (DFS) and locoregional control (LRC). Results PNI was identified in 34 of 100 evaluable patients; binary comparison showed a non-significant trend toward inferior DFS (p = 0.104) and no LRC difference (p = 0.490). Among 30 of the 34 PNI-positive patients with complete morphological data (11 DFS events; median follow-up 20.7 months), nerve diameter >429 µm was the strongest predictor of DFS (HR 3.96, 95% CI 1.18–13.02, p = 0.026), and the most consistently selected variable in LASSO bootstrap resampling (64.8%). Large nerve calibre (P1), an extratumoral component (P3) and intraneural mitoses (P5) co-occurred as an aggressive triad (pairwise φ 0.52–0.61). The composite 0–6 score was associated with DFS (HR 1.34 per point, 95% CI 1.01–1.77, p = 0.044) and stratified patients into low-risk (0–2) and high-risk (3–6) groups for DFS (p = 0.003) and LRC (p = 0.045). Conclusions PNI in node-negative OSCC is biologically significant and prognostically influential even within this favourable-prognosis (pN0, R0) subgroup; quantitative morphological characterisation, particularly of invaded nerve diameter, adds prognostic information beyond binary reporting. A composite morphological score may identify PNI-positive patients for future prospective evaluation of risk-adapted adjuvant strategies; external multicentre validation is required before clinical application.

Integrative single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analysis identifies monocyte/macrophage senescence-associated candidate genes in pulmonary arterial hypertension
abstractText: Background Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a progressive vascular disorder characterized by immune dysregulation and vascular remodeling. Cellular senescence modulates immune responses, but its role in PAH, particularly in monocytes/macrophages, remains unclear. Here, we integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify senescence-associated candidate genes associated with monocytes/macrophages in PAH. Methods Publicly available single-cell RNA-seq data from PAH and control pulmonary vascular tissues were analyzed. A senescence-associated score was calculated for each cell based on MSigDB gene sets. Senescence-associated genes in monocytes/macrophages were identified through correlation and differential expression screening, and further examined in bulk transcriptomic datasets. Bulk transcriptomic discovery used GSE113439, GSE117261, and GSE254617. A sample-title audit identified 68 shared PHBI identifiers between GSE117261 and GSE254617; therefore, the merged data represented 257 expression profiles from 189 unique subjects. LASSO, Random Forest, and XGBoost were used as complementary feature-selection approaches, and genes jointly retained by the three algorithms were defined as candidates for evaluation in independent cohorts. Results Single-cell RNA-seq identified 14 cell types in PAH pulmonary vascular tissues, with dendritic cells, T cells, and monocytes/macrophages exhibiting the highest senescence-associated scores. Integrative screening identified 405 senescence-associated genes enriched in monocytes/macrophages. Multi-algorithm screening prioritized 10 candidate genes for subsequent evaluation. After within-cohort multiple-testing correction, external cohort analyses reproduced the discovery-stage expression directions for RGS1 , PHLDA1 , MAFB , and RNF13 in lung tissue cohorts, and for MAFB in a PBMC cohort. With nominal P values, RGS1 was significantly upregulated in GSE48149 and GSE53408 (both lung), and PHLDA1 was upregulated in GSE48149 (lung). MAFB was significantly downregulated in GSE33463 (PBMC) and GSE48149 (lung), whereas RNF13 was downregulated in GSE15197 and GSE48149 (both lung). Functional analysis revealed significant enrichment of immune-inflammatory and phagocytosis-related pathways among the candidate genes. Consensus clustering based on the candidate genes classified PAH patients into two exploratory transcriptomic groups with distinct expression and pathway activity profiles. In vivo evaluation in an MCT-induced PAH rat model showed seven significant direction-consistent changes, two direction-consistent nonsignificant trends, and one discordant gene ( PDE4B ), supporting tissue-level expression concordance. Conclusion These analyses identify a Mono.Macs-associated senescence-related candidate gene set in PAH. Independent expression analyses provide additional support for RGS1 , PHLDA1 , MAFB , and RNF13 as candidate genes for subsequent mechanistic and functional validation.

title: Generative AI-Powered Interdisciplinary Chemistry Practice in Junior High: Exploring Matter Composition and Structure
abstractText: To address persistent issues in junior high chemistry teaching of Composition and Structure of Substances—including fragmented disciplinary perspectives, highly abstract micro-level concepts, and underdeveloped macro-submicro-symbolic triple representation thinking—this study constructs a four-stage interdisciplinary practical teaching model integrated with generative artificial intelligence (AI) and virtual reality (VR). The teaching practice was implemented in a natural ninth-grade class (N=40) in Zhengzhou. To ensure in-depth analysis of the massive multimodal data generated by AI and VR interactions, purposive sampling was employed to select five representative students as a focus group. Following a single-group pretest-posttest design, data from this focus group were evaluated across four dimensions to systematically measure learning outcomes: macro cognition via concept maps, micro cognition via knowledge cards, model deepening through AI text error correction, and transfer competence and AI literacy via AI chat record coding. Post-intervention data revealed significant improvements across all dimensions. In macro cognition, average concept map nodes increased by 108.8% (from 6.8 to 14.2). For micro cognition, accuracy scores of micro-level tasks surged by 170.0% (from 1.0 to 2.7). Furthermore, the error correction rate reached 88.9% during model refinement, while critical probing questions accounted for 45.83% of total chat records, indicating enhanced transfer and AI literacy. These findings confirm that the generative AI-empowered interdisciplinary model effectively broadens students’ cognitive frameworks, lowers learning barriers of abstract chemical knowledge, consolidates mastery of model-based symbolic representation, and fosters preliminary AI critical literacy. It provides a practical, replicable reference for advancing digital interdisciplinary chemistry teaching at the junior high level.

With whom you elaborate matters: how learning orientation impacts cross-culture and same-culture information elaboration in culturally diverse teams
abstractText: Abstract Work teams are increasingly characterized by diverse cultural backgrounds. Although research has established that cultural diversity holds the potential to enhance team performance through information elaboration—the exchange, discussion, and integration of task-relevant information—prior work has treated elaboration as an undifferentiated process, leaving unspecified whether it occurs across or within cultural boundaries. We develop a differentiated elaboration perspective that distinguishes cross-culture information elaboration between culturally dissimilar members from same-culture information elaboration between culturally similar members. Using a multi-source, multi-wave study of 104 culturally diverse teams comprising 587 members, we found that, as expected, cross-culture elaboration was more strongly related to team performance than same-culture elaboration. Moreover, team learning orientation predicted both forms of elaboration, and its indirect association with team performance was stronger through cross-culture elaboration. These findings advance a differentiated elaboration perspective to demonstrate that elaboration that crosses cultural boundaries is more important for diverse teams than same-culture elaboration. This points to opportunities for future research on reaping the benefits of diverse teams.

title: Sex differences in sleep and memory relationships in older adults at risk for Alzheimer’s disease
abstractText: Introduction Biological sex is an important modifier of aging and Alzheimer’s disease risk, yet the sleep-related mechanisms through which sex and genetic risk interact to influence memory remain poorly understood. We examined whether associations among non-rapid eye movement sleep physiology, overnight memory retention, and apolipoprotein E ϵ4 ( APOE ϵ4) status, a genetic risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease, differed by sex in cognitively unimpaired older adults enriched for Alzheimer’s disease risk. Methods Eighty participants completed overnight polysomnography with high-density electroencephalography, and 65 also completed an evening encoding/immediate recall and morning delayed recall word-pair memory task. Results Overnight memory retention did not differ by sex. However, exploratory analyses of the proportional overnight retention measure suggested a sex × APOE ϵ4 interaction, such that female APOE ϵ4 carriers may exhibit reduced overnight forgetting relative to female non-carriers and male carriers. Although counterintuitive, this pattern may reflect compensatory or resilience-related sleep-memory mechanisms in cognitively unimpaired women at genetic risk for Alzheimer’s disease rather than a protective effect of APOE ϵ4 itself. Women spent more time in N3 sleep and had higher non-rapid eye movement delta and slow sigma power than men. Sleep-memory associations also differed by sex: greater N2 duration was more strongly associated with better overnight retention in men, whereas greater frontal slow sigma power and fronto-central fast sigma power were positively associated with retention in women. Exploratory APOE-stratified analyses suggested sex-specific differences in sleep stage-memory relationships, with more positive N2-memory associations in male than female APOE ϵ4 carriers and more positive N3-memory associations in female than male carriers; both differences remained significant after FDR correction. TFCE-corrected analyses further identified positive associations between NREM delta and sigma activity and overnight memory retention in female APOE ϵ4 carriers. Discussion These findings highlight sex-specific patterns in NREM sleep physiology and sleep-memory relationships in cognitively unimpaired older adults at risk for Alzheimer’s disease. More broadly, the results suggest that sex and APOE ϵ4 status may jointly shape the neurophysiological pathways linking sleep and memory, underscoring the importance of considering sex as a biological variable when studying sleep, cognitive aging, and Alzheimer’s disease vulnerability.

title: Pendampingan NIB dan Sertifikasi Halal bagi Pelaku UMKM di Desa Ngalas, Kabupaten Klaten
abstractText: Business legality is essential for strengthening the sustainability and competitiveness of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). However, some MSME actors in Ngalas Village, Klaten Regency, still face difficulties obtaining a Business Identification Number (NIB) and Halal Certification. This community service program aimed to assist MSMEs in applying for both documents through a Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach. Activities included problem identification, observation, interviews, business data collection, program planning, workshops, technical assistance, and monitoring. The program involved students from KKN Groups 091 and 092, the village government, MSME actors, and Halalan Tayyiban Center as a technical partner. The main workshop was held on July 11, 2026, at Ngalas Village Hall, followed by visits to verify business data and collect product samples. Participants received practical guidance on document preparation and application procedures through the OSS and SiHalal systems. At the end of the KKN period, document issuance remained ongoing. Follow-up monitoring through a WhatsApp group maintained communication with the technical partner and supported application completion and program sustainability.

title: Association between mandibular plane angle and mandibular condylar head volume in adults with skeletal Class III deformity indicated for orthognathic surgery: a CBCT study
abstractText: Abstract Background Mandibular condylar morphology varies with craniofacial pattern, but the association between mandibular plane angle (MPA) and specifically defined condylar head volume in skeletally mature adults with skeletal Class III deformity remains insufficiently characterized. This study evaluated that association in patients indicated for orthognathic surgery. Methods This retrospective, cross-sectional, single-center study included 66 adults (33 males and 33 females; 18–40 years), with 22 patients each classified as hypodivergent (MPA < 26°), normodivergent (26°–38°), or hyperdivergent (> 38°). Bilateral condylar head volumes were measured on preoperative CBCT images using manual three-dimensional segmentation. Patient-level mean bilateral volume was used for unadjusted group comparisons with Welch ANOVA and Games–Howell tests. The primary analysis used a linear mixed-effects model with patient-specific random intercepts to account for bilateral correlation; MPA was analyzed continuously with adjustment for age, sex, and side. Results Mean bilateral condylar head volume was 1760.1 ± 476.9 mm³ in hypodivergent, 1448.8 ± 264.1 mm³ in normodivergent, and 983.1 ± 325.5 mm³ in hyperdivergent patients (Welch ANOVA, F(2, 40.13) = 23.24; p < 0.001); all pairwise comparisons were significant. In the mixed-effects model, each 1° increase in MPA was associated with a 31.91 mm³ decrease in condylar head volume (β = −31.91 mm³/°, 95% CI − 41.64 to − 22.18; p < 0.001). Female sex was associated with lower volume (β = −318.51 mm³, 95% CI − 484.58 to − 152.43; p < 0.001), and left-sided condyles with greater volume (β = 101.70 mm³, 95% CI 41.06 to 162.35; p = 0.001). Age was not associated with volume ( p = 0.744). Robust GEE sensitivity analysis yielded consistent findings. Conclusions Higher MPA was independently associated with smaller condylar head volume in this selected surgical Class III cohort. The cross-sectional, single-center design does not establish causality or support generalization to all individuals with skeletal Class III malocclusion.

title: Definitive radiotherapy versus surgery after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma: a propensity score-matched study of efficacy and safety
abstractText: Background The optimal local treatment strategy for locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (LA-ESCC) following neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT) remains controversial. This study aimed to compare the survival outcomes and recurrence patterns of radical surgery and definitive radiotherapy (RT) following NICT in patients with LA-ESCC. Methods Patients with LA-ESCC who underwent NICT (2019–2023) were enrolled and categorized into surgery or RT groups. Propensity score matching (PSM) and Kaplan-Meier methods were used to estimate progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS). The differences in recurrence patterns between the two groups were compared. Results A total of 278 patients were included, comprising 218 (78.4%) and 60 (21.6%) patients in the surgery and RT groups, respectively. After PSM, the surgery group (n=117) maintained a significant OS benefit over the RT group (n=60) (3-year OS rates: 72.1% vs. 59.5%; P = 0.028), whereas the PFS rates were comparable between the two groups (3-year PFS rates: 59.4% vs. 46.9%; P = 0.12). For patients with upper esophageal cancer, RT showed a trend toward improved survival (3-year PFS rates: 76.9% vs. 55.5%, P = 0.34; 3-year OS rates: 74.0% vs. 61.8%, P = 0.50). Among the responders after NICT (near-cCR/cPR), PFS and OS were similar between the surgery and RT groups (3-year PFS rates: 68.9% vs. 66.9%, P = 0.64; 3-year OS rates: 80.2% vs. 70.7%, P = 0.20). Regional lymph node recurrence predominated in the surgery group (50.0%), whereas locoregional esophageal recurrence was most frequent in the RT group (37.0%). The treatment-related mortality rates were 0.8% (1/117) in the surgery group and 1.7% (1/60) in the RT group, indicating the overall safety of the treatments. Conclusions Radical surgery remains the standard treatment for LA-ESCC after NICT. Definitive RT may be an organ-preserving option in selected patients, especially those with upper esophageal cancer or a favorable response to NICT.

title: A scoping review and conceptual framework mapping the determinants of malaria vaccine acceptance among adults in Africa
abstractText: Abstract Background Malaria remains a severe public health crisis in Africa, causing 94% of global cases and 95% of deaths in 2023. While the rollout of the RTS, S/AS01 and R21/Matrix-M vaccines marks a historic shift, long-term public health success relies on adult acceptance particularly among parents, caregivers, and healthcare workers amid rising vaccine hesitancy. This scoping review systematically identified and classified the determinants of malaria vaccine acceptance and hesitancy among adults in Africa using the Health Belief Model (HBM) and the World Health Organization Strategic Advisory Group of Experts (WHO SAGE) Vaccine Hesitancy Matrix, presenting the operationalized proposed conceptual framework to guide future rollout strategies. Methods Guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) checklist, six electronic databases (PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, AJOL, CINAHL, and PsycINFO) and grey literature sources were searched for literature published from January 2019 to July 2025. Studies exploring adult perceptions, barriers, and facilitators toward malaria vaccination in Africa were screened. Deductive thematic content analysis was applied to map findings across HBM constructs and WHO SAGE domains. Results Out of 3000 retrieved records, 30 studies met the strict inclusion criteria, comprising 25 peer-reviewed articles and 5 grey literature reports across 13 African countries. High baseline vaccine willingness rates (> 80%) were primarily driven by trust in healthcare providers (26.7% of studies), high perceived malaria severity (23.3%), and community engagement workshops (16.7%). Conversely, critical barriers to uptake included deep-seated misinformation and infertility rumors (16.7%), fear of vaccine side effects (23.3%), complex multi-dose schedules (23.3%), and logistical or cold-chain constraints (16.7%). These determinants were successfully synthesized into three key operational domains: Contextual, Individual/Group, and Vaccine-Specific Influences. Conclusion Addressing structural and psychological barriers requires evidence-informed, culturally sensitive interventions. National Ministries of Health should prioritize community-led health education, integrate trusted religious and local figures to counteract misinformation, and reinforce cold-chain infrastructure to ensure equitable delivery.

title: HUBUNGAN RIWAYAT ASI, WAKTU MPASI, DAN ASUPAN MAKRONUTRIEN DENGAN PERTUMBUHAN ANAK DI KASIHAN
abstractText: ABSTRACT Child growth is an important indicator of health status and is influenced by feeding history and adequate nutrient intake. This study aimed to analyze the associations of breastfeeding history, timing of complementary feeding (MPASI), and carbohydrate and protein intake with the growth status of children aged 4–6 years at two ABA kindergartens in Kasihan District. This study used an analytical observational design with a cross-sectional approach and retrospective assessment of breastfeeding and complementary feeding history. A total of 66 children were included as research subjects. Breastfeeding and complementary feeding histories were obtained using questionnaires, carbohydrate and protein intake were assessed using food records, and growth status was determined through anthropometric measurements, including height-for-age (HAZ), weight-for-age (WAZ), and weight-for-height (WHZ). The statistical analysis showed no significant associations between breastfeeding history, timing of complementary feeding, and carbohydrate intake and the growth indicators assessed (p>0.05). Similarly, the association between protein intake and height-for-age was not statistically significant based on Fisher’s exact test (p=0.106). Descriptively, most children had a history of exclusive breastfeeding (86.4%), received complementary feeding at the appropriate age (90.9%), had adequate carbohydrate intake (90.9%), and had adequate protein intake (98.5%). Most children also had normal or good growth status based on the anthropometric indicators assessed. In conclusion, breastfeeding history, timing of complementary feeding, carbohydrate intake, and protein intake were not significantly associated with the growth status of children aged 4–6 years in the study population. ABSTRAK Pertumbuhan anak merupakan salah satu indikator penting status kesehatan dan dipengaruhi oleh riwayat pemberian makan serta kecukupan asupan zat gizi. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis hubungan riwayat pemberian air susu ibu (ASI), waktu pemberian makanan pendamping ASI (MPASI), serta asupan karbohidrat dan protein dengan status pertumbuhan anak usia 4–6 tahun di dua TK ABA Kecamatan Kasihan. Penelitian ini menggunakan desain observasional analitik dengan pendekatan cross-sectional dan penilaian retrospektif terhadap riwayat pemberian ASI dan MPASI. Sebanyak 66 anak diikutsertakan sebagai subjek penelitian. Riwayat ASI dan MPASI diperoleh melalui kuesioner, asupan karbohidrat dan protein dinilai menggunakan food record, sedangkan status pertumbuhan ditentukan berdasarkan pengukuran antropometri meliputi tinggi badan menurut usia (TB/U), berat badan menurut usia (BB/U), dan berat badan menurut tinggi badan (BB/TB). Hasil analisis menunjukkan bahwa tidak terdapat hubungan yang bermakna antara riwayat ASI, waktu pemberian MPASI, dan asupan karbohidrat dengan indikator status pertumbuhan yang diteliti (p>0,05). Demikian pula, hubungan antara asupan protein dan TB/U tidak menunjukkan hasil yang bermakna berdasarkan Fisher’s exact test (p=0,106). Secara deskriptif, sebagian besar anak memiliki riwayat ASI eksklusif (86,4%), menerima MPASI sesuai usia (90,9%), memiliki asupan karbohidrat baik (90,9%), dan asupan protein baik (98,5%), dengan sebagian besar indikator pertumbuhan berada dalam kategori normal atau baik. Dengan demikian, riwayat pemberian ASI dan MPASI serta asupan karbohidrat dan protein tidak menunjukkan hubungan yang signifikan dengan status pertumbuhan anak usia 4–6 tahun pada populasi penelitian.

title: Enhancing Student Motivation and Academic Achievement through Interactive Video Lessons in Workplace English
abstractText: This study addresses the persistent challenge faced by university students in maintaining motivation and achieving proficiency in complex Workplace English, a context where traditional instruction often falls short. We examined whether incorporating interactive video lessons could offer a more engaging learning experience. A mixed-methods research design was implemented over one academic semester with a cohort of junior students enrolled in a compulsory English course. The intervention utilized the iSLCollective platform to customize video content by embedding interactive questions and tasks into existing lessons from an established English language teaching resource. Data were gathered through pre- and post-intervention English proficiency assessments, complemented by motivational surveys measuring goal orientation, task value, control beliefs, and self-efficacy. Quantitative analyses revealed notable positive trends and statistically significant gains in both student motivation and academic achievement. Participants reported increased drive to learn, alongside greater confidence in mastering the material. Qualitative feedback further highlighted that interactive questions, immediate feedback, and gamified elements were favorably received by students. These findings suggest that interactive multimedia tools can serve as a promising auxiliary approach to enhance learner engagement and support second language acquisition. Future research incorporating control groups should explore the long-term impact of this approach across broader educational settings.

title: Synchrony in neural and visceral systems: a bioelectric basis of consciousness
abstractText: The Default Space Theory (DST) of consciousness claims that consciousness arises from bioelectric oscillations across brain and body which become time-locked to form an internal three-dimensionalized “default space” which continuously simulates external reality. Within this frame, we assert that fast rhythms created corticothalamically with the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) can become time-locked with regions throughout the brain via nascent oscillations as well as sensory organs and viscera. This proposed time-locking may render exteroceptive and interoceptive processed information one in the same as conscious experience. We review/integrate salient neuroscientific and physiological findings that validate DST. We reveal findings across the last decoding of the theory's detailed components from corticothalamic feedback loops to lateral/inhibition dynamics, from descending efferent projections to sensory organs. We utilize high cervical cord injury (HCCI) as syndromically supporting/denying DST's postulates regarding the necessity of bodily input to consciousness. Finally, we compare/contrast theories (Global Workspace, Integrated Information Theory, Predictive Processing) with DST to reveal overlaps/distinctions within theoretical scaffolds. At its heart, the DST is an all-encompassing biological apparatus through which typical oscillations create a “functional unity” of consciousness. Yet developments within the DST have brought about clarity that simultaneous connected long distances (i.e., gamma oscillations aligning cortex to sensory receptors) is a theory to be born out of experimentation, not reality. There is indirect support from visual studies for retinal rhythmic activity driving thalamocortical firing in a way consistent with modulation but direct phase-locking of periphery receptors with gamma activity in the cortex is aspirational, not reality. In addition, we corrected a prior disconnection regarding motor representations: focus of outputs occurs by surround inhibition (SI) eliminating superfluous irrelevant activations, not the cortical silent period—thus when SI fails there is motor “overflow.” We further clarify the importance of viscera in conscious experience with several examples: spontaneous breathing aligns electrical oscillations in limbo circuits, heart beats are shown to engage/disengage cortical activity and awareness, gastric slow waves correlate in-phase with what occurs in somatosensory and visual domains. All support DST positing that the neural and visceral systems operate as one oscillator network which, together, support consciousness. In an HCCI patient where somatic input below the neck is deceased, however, they experience retained consciousness, however. This DST predicts because oscillations of the head/brain and rhythms from the viscera allow continuity of internal space; yet its content/persona changes because the body map has been temporally truncated. This provides a distinction about how people can be consciously aware of their existence while feeling completely different at the same time—there is a core conscious sense vs. the schemas decorating it over timescales. The DST provides a bioelectric understanding of consciousness which connects brain-body-environment. Where we emphasize where theoretical estimations lie vs. what can be observed supports the DST. For example, if one excessively disrupts corticothalamic feedback loops or sensorimotor oscillations and fails to integrate things into consciousness, DST is supported. Conversely, these stimulus distortions will never come from any other theoretical premise. Prominent notions are shared with Global Workspace or Integrated Information-based systems regarding global integration, but no other theory has included the body's oscillatory components as part of consciousness; contrary to predictive processing, while prediction errors determine hypotheses, DST puts forward simultaneous synchronization as critical and afferent/efferent dynamics physicalized two-way brain-body communication. Testing factors inevitable in evolution include consistent electrophysiological studies with descending pathways, works decoding states of consciousness in paralysis. All citations updated for relevancy—new studies incorporated—non-self-citations limited to remove experimenter's bias—all to urge ongoing discourse between DST and contemporaneous science of consciousness research.

NeuroEarlyAI: An Explainable Deep Learning Framework with EarlyDetectNet for Alzheimer’s Disease Detection and Classification using MRI Scans
abstractText: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is an ageing and progressive neurodegenerative disease, and one of the most prevalent dementias that affects millions of patients worldwide, including millions of people in Europe, and is a public health priority. Early and right diagnosis is of paramount importance for early therapeutic intervention as well as retardation of the disease. The visual search for small changes in the brain is rather time-consuming and subjective. For comparison, we chose two traditional diagnostic procedures: clinical evaluation and manual MRI analysis, where the clinical evaluation is more appropriate for the intended user in healthcare centres. The automatic detection of AD using recent advancements in deep learning are yet to lack a few drawbacks, such as class imbalance, overfitting and generalisation issue on external datasets, low transparency in the decision-making of the deep learning model, which makes it difficult for clinical applications. To fill this gap, in this paper, we propose NeuroEarlyAI, an end-to-end learning framework with EarlyDetectNet, a new model for early and interpretable detection of AD from the structural MRI scans. The framework also consists of sophisticated pre-processing strategies (denoising, data augmentation and skull stripping) to enhance the quality and diversity of the data. EarlyDetectNet has an attention mechanism which highlights clinically relevant anatomical regions. As a contrast, the visual and feature-wise explanation modules are based on the Grad-CAM and SHAP techniques, respectively, which project the model prediction onto the visual and feature-wise explanations. Extensive tests are performed on two publicly available datasets: Alzheimer's MRI Dataset and OASIS-1 dataset. The proposed system demonstrated improvements over the state of the art on reaching accuracy for binary and multi-class classification in a cross-dataset setting, with 96.7% and 93.8% accuracy, respectively. These results show the promise of the applications and broader use of NeuroEarlyAI, a tool that could help to diagnose AD earlier for better patient care.

Anesthesiological considerations and complications in robotic surgery: a retrospective analysis
abstractText: Abstract Robotic-assisted surgery has become increasingly prevalent across various surgical disciplines. Understanding anesthesiological factors influencing perioperative outcome is essential for optimizing patient care. This retrospective analysis evaluated 200 patients who underwent robotic surgery across three surgical categories: gastrointestinal (GI, n=60), hepatopancreticobiliary (HPB, n=28), and colorectal (n=112) procedures. We conducted an exploratory analysis of associations between anesthesiological parameters—including fluid management, surgical duration, and blood loss—and clinical outcomes such as intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay, total hospital length of stay, complication severity (Clavien-Dindo classification) using univariable and multivariable regression models. The exploratory analyses suggested potential associations between surgical duration and outcomes across surgical specialties in multivariable analysis. For GI procedures, longer surgical duration was associated with higher odds of severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III; OR = 1.80 (1.21, 2.66)). In colorectal surgery, surgical duration was independently associated with both development of severe complications (OR = 1.28 (1.01, 1.62)) and total hospital length of stay (log-scale, β = 0.08 (0.03, 0.12)). Fluid intake was associated with an increased hospital length of stay in colorectal surgery (log-scale, β = 0.10 (0.03, 0.17)). Anesthesiological management, particularly surgical duration and fluid management, showed associations with perioperative outcomes in robotic surgery. The estimated effects provide preliminary insights into the magnitude of these associations and may serve as a basis for hypothesis generation and the design of future prospective studies. Further studies are needed to confirm these findings and to investigate the potential clinical relevance of anesthesiological and perioperative management strategies.

title: Nursing students’ attitudes towards mental illness and mental health nursing education at Hanoi Medical University
abstractText: Objective: To describe nursing students’ attitudes towards mental illness and mental health nursing education and examine correlations among attitude domains at Hanoi Medical University. Methods: A descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted among 81 nursing students (response rate: 53%) who had completed both theoretical and clinical components of the mental health nursing course. Attitudes were assessed using the Mental Health Nurse Education Survey (MHNES). Results: Most students were willing to care for people with mental illness in the same way as other patients (91.4%) and agreed that mental health nursing contributes positively to care (90.2%) and supports recovery (90.1%). Overall, 74.1% reported that theoretical education prepared them well for clinical placement, and 87.7% considered the clinical placement valuable for nursing practice. After graduation, 85.2% intended to further develop their mental health knowledge and skills, although 40.7% reported anxiety about working with people with mental health problems, and only 24.7% intended to pursue a career in mental health nursing. Preparedness for the mental health field was positively correlated with knowledge (r = 0.25, p < 0.05), perceived positive contribution (r = 0.49, p < 0.01), course effectiveness (r = 0.76, p < 0.01) and negatively correlated with negative stereotypes (r = −0.26, p < 0.05). The correlations with knowledge and negative stereotypes did not remain significant after Bonferroni adjustment. Conclusion: Participating nursing students generally demonstrated positive attitudes towards mental illness and mental health nursing education, although anxiety and negative stereotypes persisted. Although the associations were cross-sectional, educational strategies should focus on reducing stigma and strengthening students’ preparedness for mental health care.

title: Procedural interventions for chronic migraine: an umbrella review intervention-specific evidence map
abstractText: Objective To synthesize and map intervention-specific evidence on the efficacy, clinical relevance, and safety of procedural interventions for chronic migraine (CM). Methods We conducted a PROSPERO-registered umbrella review in accordance with PRISMA 2020 and methodological guidance for umbrella reviews. Eligible systematic reviews evaluated onabotulinumtoxinA, greater occipital nerve block (GONB), other peripheral nerve blocks and percutaneous procedures, acupuncture, implanted occipital nerve stimulation (ONS), or surgical interventions. Evidence concerning the addition of CGRP-targeted monoclonal antibody therapy to ongoing onabotulinumtoxinA treatment was retained separately as contextual evidence on adjunctive pharmacotherapy and was not classified as a procedural intervention. Methodological quality was assessed using A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), certainty of evidence using Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE), and primary-study overlap using the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence was synthesized separately by intervention, outcome, comparator, and follow-up period. Pooled estimates from different systematic reviews were not statistically combined, and clinically heterogeneous evidence was summarized narratively. Results Seventeen reviews were included, of which 12 contained at least one meta-analysis. The strength and maturity of evidence varied substantially across interventions. OnabotulinumtoxinA had the most established evidence base and the clearest role in CM prevention. For GONB, low-certainty evidence from clinically comparable randomized trials suggested a possible short-term reduction in headache day and headache severity, although sustained benefit remains uncertain. Evidence for combined onabotulinumtoxinA–CGRP monoclonal antibody therapy was derived predominantly from uncontrolled observational cohorts and should therefore be considered preliminary. Implanted ONS showed possible benefit in selected patients with refractory CM, but evidence was limited by small study numbers, imprecision, heterogeneous outcomes, and device- or procedure-related risks. Evidence for acupuncture, other peripheral nerve blocks, percutaneous procedures, and surgical interventions was limited by clinical heterogeneity, indirectness, uncontrolled study designs, or uncertain applicability specifically to CM. TRAEs profiles differed substantially among intervention categories and were therefore not pooled across procedures. Most intervention–outcome evidence was rated as low or very low certainty. Conclusions Procedural interventions for CM should not be interpreted as a homogeneous therapeutic class. OnabotulinumtoxinA is supported by the most mature evidence and established clinical positioning, whereas GONB may provide a short-term, protocol-specific benefit with low certainty. Evidence for other procedures remains preliminary, heterogeneous, or restricted to selected patient populations. Clinical interpretation and treatment selection should therefore be intervention-specific and patient-specific. Future research should prioritize standardized diagnostic criteria, treatment protocols, comparators, clinically meaningful outcomes, TRAEs reporting, and longer-term follow-up. Too Hot, Too Cold, or Just Right? The Effects of Temperature on Sleep
abstractText: Sleep is necessary for optimal functioning and for overall health and wellbeing. You might have heard advice on how to improve your sleep, such as reducing intense activities close to bedtime or keeping a regular sleep-and-wake schedule. As many countries experience climate change, it is also important to be aware of how sleep may be affected when the temperature changes. Sleep may be delayed or disturbed in a cold environment or a hot and humid one, and poor sleep can make it difficult to function well, especially if it happens often. It is important to create a good sleep environment, keeping in mind that the temperature and humidity of the room, the air circulation, as well as the bedding and clothes worn to bed, play a role in a person’s ability to get the most out of the time spent in bed.
