Delivery Accuracy, Robotics, and Logistics Information System Integration in Operational Performance Through Sorting Optimization
abstractText: Background: Logistics transformation at Sentral Pengolahan Pos (SPP) Jakarta, a high-volume mail-processing hub within PT Pos Indonesia (Persero), is taking place amid rising shipment volumes and persistent challenges in national logistics performance. Objective: This study examines the relationships between delivery accuracy, robotic technology implementation, and logistics information system integration and logistics operational performance, with sorting process optimization tested as a mediating variable. Method: The study employed a quantitative explanatory, cross-sectional design using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. Primary data were collected through a 5-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered to 80 employees and operators at SPP Jakarta using total sampling (census). Results: All ten hypothesized structural paths were statistically supported. Delivery accuracy, robotic technology implementation, and logistics information system integration were positively and significantly associated with sorting process optimization and logistics operational performance. Robotic technology implementation showed the largest path coefficient for sorting process optimization (0.471), while logistics information system integration showed the largest direct path coefficient for logistics operational performance (0.434). Sorting process optimization demonstrated statistically significant but limited partial mediation, with Variance Accounted For (VAF) values ranging from 20.31% to 26.05%, indicating that most of the modeled relationships remained direct rather than being transmitted through the mediator. Conclusion: The findings suggest that PT Pos Indonesia should strengthen robotic technology utilization, information system interoperability, and sorting process optimization as complementary operational capabilities. Because the data are cross-sectional and perception-based, the results should be interpreted as structural associations rather than definitive causal effects.

title: IMPLEMENTASI SISTEM INFORMASI PENGELOLAAN TRANSAKSI DAN PEMBUKUAN BERBASIS WEB UNTUK UMKM PENGEPUL BARANG RONGSOKAN (STUDI KASUS: PAK IYAN, RAWALUMBU)
abstractText: MSMEs engaged in scrap collection play a role in supporting the circular economy through the collection, sorting, and resale of used materials to recycling industries. One such business, owned by Pak Iyan in Rawalumbu, Bekasi, still records purchase and sales transactions using a simple notebook, making the records prone to errors and data loss and making it difficult to determine the financial condition of the business and monitor fluctuations in scrap prices. This study aims to analyze the requirements, design, implement, test, and evaluate the implementation of a simple web-based accounting information system for Pak Iyan's business. The study employed a development research method with a case study approach and qualitative descriptive and simple quantitative descriptive analyses. Data were collected through observation, interviews, and documentation of business processes and user requirements. The system was developed using a no-code/low-code approach, with Canva as the interface, Google Forms as the data input medium, and Google Sheets as the data storage and processing medium. The developed system includes recording purchase and sales transactions, automatically calculating transaction totals, preparing a simple cash-basis profit and loss report, and monitoring historical fluctuations in scrap prices. The functional testing results show that 4 of 7 features (57%) were successfully tested directly, including sales transactions, transaction total calculations, scrap price fluctuation monitoring, and the system interface. The implementation evaluation showed an average improvement in recording time efficiency of 87.5% and positive user feedback. These results indicate that the system can help Pak Iyan record transactions in a more structured and efficient manner compared with the previous manual recording method.

Reduced contrast volume in coronary CT angiography: effects on coronary attenuation
abstractText: Abstract Background Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) requires intravenous iodinated contrast to achieve diagnostic intraluminal opacification. Because reducing the contrast volume administered per examination is an exposure-reduction strategy of practical interest, institutions have explored lower-volume protocols; whether attenuation can be preserved above the diagnostic threshold under real-world, non-randomized implementation is not well documented outside research settings. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, non-concurrent before-and-after protocol-implementation study was conducted at Radiology Center (January 2023–December 2024). From 200 CCTA examinations initially identified from radiology reports as potentially eligible, 106 were excluded (44 body weight >120 kg; 12 beta-blocker administered; 27 coronary calcification/calcium scoring without significant stenosis; 23 motion artefact), leaving 94 CT-angiographically normal examinations: 51 under the standard (pre-reduction) protocol and 43 under the reduced-volume (post-reduction) protocol. All examinations used a third-generation dual-source CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM Force) with automated tube-voltage selection (CARE kV) and tube-current modulation (CARE Dose4D), retrospective ECG gating, and a 32-cm scan length. Omnipaque 350 mgI/mL was administered by power injector with bolus tracking (ascending aorta ROI, 90 HU trigger, 5 s post-trigger delay). Intraluminal attenuation was measured by a single reader in the left main trunk (LMT) and proximal right coronary artery (RCA); no inter- or intra-observer reproducibility assessment was performed. Distributions were assessed with the Shapiro–Wilk test; normally distributed variables were compared with the independent-samples (Welch) t-test and non-normally distributed variables with the Mann–Whitney U test. A multivariable linear model examined coronary attenuation as a function of protocol epoch, kVp, body weight, heart rate, and iodine delivery rate. Results Contrast volume fell from 63.4 ± 7.3 mL to 49.0 ± 8.0 mL (median 60 [IQR 60–65] vs 45 [45–52.5] mL), a 22.8% reduction (Mann–Whitney p < 0.001), with a corresponding 22.8% reduction in iodine mass (22.20 ± 2.56 vs 17.13 ± 2.79 gI). Iodine delivery rate was essentially unchanged (1.69 ± 0.14 vs 1.69 ± 0.14 gI/s; p = 0.91). Mean LMT attenuation decreased from 520.4 ± 93.6 HU to 451.9 ± 90.7 HU (− 13.2%; t-test p < 0.001) and mean RCA attenuation from 500.2 ± 107.1 HU to 418.1 ± 89.3 HU (− 16.4%; Mann–Whitney p < 0.001). At the per-patient level, 41/43 post-reduction examinations (95.3%; exact 95% CI 84.2–99.4%) reached ≥ 300 HU at the LMT and 39/43 (90.7%; 95% CI 77.9–97.4%) at the RCA; 4/43 examinations, therefore, fell below the SCCT diagnostic threshold at the RCA and 2/43 at the LMT. In the multivariable model, protocol epoch remained independently associated with lower attenuation after adjustment for kVp, weight, heart rate, and iodine delivery rate (LMT: β = − 75.7 HU, 95% CI − 111.6 to − 39.8, p < 0.001; RCA: β = − 87.8 HU, 95% CI − 128.0 to − 47.7, p < 0.001). Mean DLP was 1158.2 ± 637.4 mGy·cm (pre) versus 1072.1 ± 530.6 mGy·cm (post), a non-significant 7.4% difference (Mann–Whitney p = 0.71); the reduction in DLP standard deviation (16.8%) corresponds to an estimated 30.7% reduction in variance, which was not statistically significant (Levene’s test p = 0.24). No renal function or image-quality metric was measured. Conclusion A reduced-volume contrast protocol lowered administered contrast volume and total iodine mass by 22.8% while iodine delivery rate was maintained. Mean coronary attenuation remained above 300 HU in both groups, but a per-patient minority of post-reduction examinations fell below this threshold, particularly at the RCA. Radiation-dose differences were a co-temporal secondary observation and are not attributable to the contrast protocol. Renal outcomes were not assessed, and the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of nephroprotection or as a formal non-inferiority result.

The Relationship Between Social Media Use Intensity, Body Image, and Bullying Behavior Among Vocational High School Students: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis
abstractText: Social media has reshaped peer interactions and perceptions of physical appearance among adolescents, raising concerns about body dissatisfaction and bullying. However, evidence regarding the relationships among these experiences remains fragmented, particularly among vocational high school students. This study aimed to synthesize evidence on the relationships among social media use intensity, body image, and bullying involvement while mapping the development and thematic structure of the relevant literature. A systematic review and bibliometric analysis were conducted in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Publications from January 2022 to May 2025 were identified through searches of Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed, and Google Scholar. Fifty-two studies were included, critically appraised using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal tools, and synthesized narratively. Bibliometric mapping was performed using VOSviewer and Bibliometrix. The findings indicated that intensive and appearance-focused social media use was associated with greater body dissatisfaction through social comparison and the internalization of appearance ideals. Negative body image was also associated with bullying victimization, while digital environments facilitated harmful peer interactions, including cyberbullying. Bibliometric analysis identified interconnected research themes involving social media, body image, cyberbullying, and mental health. Nevertheless, heterogeneity in measurement approaches and the predominance of cross-sectional study designs limited causal inference, while evidence specifically concerning vocational high school students remained insufficient. The review concluded that integrated approaches combining digital literacy, positive body image promotion, and bullying prevention should be considered in school settings. Future longitudinal research is needed to examine contextual differences and directly test the proposed psychological pathways linking social media use, body image, and bullying involvement among adolescents.

title: 3D numerical study of race-tracking and air entrapment phenomena in polymer filling process
abstractText: Abstract The race-tracking effect and air entrapment are two important phenomena that restrict the quality and performance of injection molded parts. This study considers two types of parts with different wall-thickness distributions. Through numerical simulations combined with experimental observations, the race-tracking effect and air entrapment phenomena during polymer melt filling in 3D cavities are investigated, with particular emphasis on the influence of the thin-to-thick wall-thickness ratio. A two-phase flow model is developed by coupling the Navier–Stokes equations with the level set equation, and is discretized using a collocated grid finite volume method and the SIMPLE algorithm is employed for pressure–velocity coupling. The results show that the proposed model can accurately predict melt front evolution in complex cavities and effectively capture the race-tracking effect and air entrapment phenomena during filling. Furthermore, the thin-to-thick wall-thickness ratio plays a crucial role in both phenomena: decreasing this ratio intensifies the race-tracking effect, and for circular cavities, also increases the trapped air area.

title: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Testing Following Pennsylvania Hearing-Targeted Screening Legislation
abstractText: BACKGROUND Congenital cytomegalovirus infection (cCMV) occurs in approximately 1/200 to 1/250 US newborns each year and can cause progressive sensorineural hearing loss. Since 2022, Pennsylvania law mandates cCMV testing for infants who fail newborn hearing screening. OBJECTIVES To assess changes in cCMV testing rates and diagnosis before and after Pennsylvania hearing-targeted legislation. METHODS Retrospective cohort study of all live births at 3 university-affiliated birth centers. We identified all infants tested for CMV at 21 days of age or younger and analyzed cCMV testing rates in pre- (January 2018-June 2022) and post- (July 2022-December 2024) legislation eras using interrupted time-series analysis. We assessed other clinical signs associated with cCMV testing using standard statistics. RESULTS The study cohort included 85 324 infants. Among 54 909 born prelegislation, 3168 (5.8%) had cCMV testing; among 30 415 born postlegislation, 3197 (10.5%) were tested. cCMV testing rates increased significantly among term (by 3.2%) and preterm infants (by 15.5%) at the beginning of the postlegislation era (P = .003 and .001, respectively). Among 5224 infants with hearing-based criteria for screening, CMV testing increased from 36.7% prelegislation to 74.0% postlegislation (P < .001). In the postlegislation period, testing associated with isolated microcephaly increased, but isolated small for gestational age–associated testing decreased. Among 61 infants diagnosed with cCMV, 16 (26.2%) were identified based on hearing criteria alone (2.3/1000 infants prelegislation, 6.0/1000 infants postlegislation, P = .04). CONCLUSIONS CMV testing and diagnosis based on hearing criteria alone increased significantly post passage of Pennsylvania hearing-targeted cCMV testing legislation, but infants tested for hearing criteria alone accounted for less than half of identified cCMV cases.

title: Etnobotani Aren (Arenga pinnata) pada Masyarakat Minangkabau di Lima Puluh Kota, Sumatera Barat
abstractText: Aren (Arenga pinnata (Wurmb) Merr.) merupakan palma multiguna yang penting bagi rumah tangga pedesaan, tetapi variasi pengetahuan pemanfaatannya pada masyarakat Minangkabau di Kabupaten Lima Puluh Kota belum terdokumentasi secara komparatif. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengidentifikasi bagian aren yang dimanfaatkan, mendeskripsikan bentuk dan cara pengolahannya, serta membandingkan frekuensi penyebutan pemanfaatan pada tiga kecamatan. Survei etnobotani deskriptif dengan komponen kualitatif dan kuantitatif dilaksanakan pada Desember 2025-Maret 2026 di Kecamatan Gunuang Omeh, Lareh Sago Halaban, dan Mungka. Sebanyak 90 responden berusia ≥40 tahun (30 responden per kecamatan) diwawancarai menggunakan pertanyaan terbuka. Data dianalisis sebagai ragam bentuk pemanfaatan dan frekuensi sitasi responden, disajikan sebagai n (%). Hasil menunjukkan 10 bagian/material aren dengan 28 bentuk pemanfaatan dalam lima kelompok utama, yaitu pangan, kerajinan, bahan bangunan/energi, pengobatan tradisional, dan kebutuhan budaya. Berdasarkan daftar pemanfaatan yang terdokumentasi, Gunuang Omeh memiliki 21 bentuk pemanfaatan, Lareh Sago Halaban 15, dan Mungka 18. Sapu ijuk paling sering disebut di Gunuang Omeh (28/30; 93,3%), sedangkan gula aren dan sapu lidi masing-masing disebut oleh 23/30 responden (76,7%) di Mungka. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa pengetahuan pemanfaatan aren tidak seragam antarlokasi meskipun berada dalam satu kabupaten. Dokumentasi berbasis frekuensi sitasi ini menyediakan dasar empiris untuk penelitian lanjutan mengenai transmisi pengetahuan, nilai ekonomi, dan konservasi aren. Sugar palm (Arenga pinnata (Wurmb) Merr.) is a multipurpose palm important to rural households, yet variation in its uses and associated knowledge among Minangkabau communities in Lima Puluh Kota Regency has not been comparatively documented. This study aimed to identify the utilized parts of sugar palm, describe their uses and processing practices, and compare citation frequencies across three districts. A descriptive ethnobotanical survey combining qualitative and quantitative components was conducted from December 2025 to March 2026 in Gunuang Omeh, Lareh Sago Halaban, and Mungka. Ninety respondents aged ≥40 years (30 per district) were interviewed using open-ended questions. Data were summarized as use-type richness and respondent citation frequency, expressed as n (%). The study documented 10 sugar-palm parts/materials and 28 use types grouped into food, handicrafts, construction/energy, traditional medicine, and cultural purposes. Based on the documented list, Gunuang Omeh had 21 use types, Lareh Sago Halaban 15, and Mungka 18. Fiber brooms were most frequently cited in Gunuang Omeh (28/30; 93.3%), while palm sugar and rib brooms were each cited by 23/30 respondents (76.7%) in Mungka. These findings indicate that sugar-palm knowledge is not uniformly distributed across communities within the same regency. Citation-frequency documentation provides an empirical baseline for further research on knowledge transmission, economic value, and sugar-palm conservation.

A possible case of water-sharing in grey-headed flying-foxes during extreme heat
abstractText: Behavioural strategies used by wildlife to mitigate thermal stress are at the forefront of ecological research as the frequency, severity, and geographic range of extreme heat increase. On 27 January 2026, grey-headed flying-foxes (Pteropus poliocephalus) were monitored from the banks of the Yarra River in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia, where the maximum air temperature reached 40.7°C. An adult flying-fox belly-dipped into the river, saturating its ventral fur before landing in a tree overhanging the river; here it proceeded to drink the water off its saturated fur. This adult bat was joined by a smaller conspecific which licked the wetted bats fur for over a minute. This research note describes an apparent water-sharing behaviour and considers whether this interaction may represent a previously undescribed social mechanism that facilitates access to water during extreme heat, particularly for vulnerable individuals.

title: Risk assessment of water treatment chemical supply disruptions in China using a synthetic water quality dataset and the Best-Worst Method
abstractText: Introduction Disruptions in the supply of water treatment chemicals can affect water quality, public health, service continuity, and the resilience of water treatment systems. A systematic method is therefore required to assess mitigation strategies under different disruption conditions. Methods A data driven multi criteria framework is developed to assess the risks associated with water treatment chemical supply disruptions in China. A synthetic water quality dataset derived from the China Water Pollution Monitoring Dataset is used to construct indicators for four dimensions: compliance and public health, service continuity, supply vulnerability, and recoverability. The synthetic dataset is used as a controlled and reproducible source for methodological evaluation rather than as direct empirical evidence from Chinese water utilities. Criteria weights are determined using the Best Worst Method, and a quantitative scoring model is applied to evaluate mitigation strategies under multiple disruption scenarios. Results Compliance receives the highest criterion weight of 0.39. Among the evaluated mitigation strategies, dual sourcing obtains the highest performance score. Its score decreases from 0.74 under lower disruption severity to 0.63 under higher disruption severity, which indicates relatively stable performance across the tested scenarios. Supplier prequalification shows moderate performance and improves under severe disruption conditions, whereas safety stock shows the largest reduction in performance. Sensitivity and robustness analyses indicate that the strategy rankings remain stable under variations in criterion weights and disruption scenarios. Discussion The results indicate that the proposed framework provides a consistent and reproducible method for comparing mitigation strategies under controlled synthetic data conditions. The findings also show how multi criteria assessment can integrate water quality, service continuity, supply vulnerability, and recoverability within a common decision model. Since the analysis is based on synthetic data, the results should be interpreted as methodological evidence rather than direct evidence of the performance of Chinese water utilities. Further validation with observed utility and chemical supply data is required before operational application.

The Hidden Curriculum of Generative AI: Institutional AI Policies and the Potential for Student Inequality
abstractText: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly integrated into higher education, prompting institutions to develop policies governing its use in teaching, learning, and assessment. Although existing discussions have emphasized academic integrity, assessment practices, and technological access, less attention has been given to the knowledge and competencies students may need to interpret and comply with institutional AI policies. This study examines how institutional GenAI policies establish explicit and implicit expectations for students and identifies potential pathways through which policy-navigation demands may contribute to educational inequality. Using comparative qualitative content analysis, publicly available policies and guidance documents from 20 purposively selected higher education institutions across the United States, Canada, United Kingdom, Australia, and South Africa were examined. The analysis considered policy permissiveness, disclosure requirements, instructor discretion, student responsibilities, AI-literacy guidance, accessibility, equity, and implicit navigation demands. Findings indicate that acceptable AI use is frequently determined at the course, instructor, or assessment level, requiring students to interpret context-specific rules, understand disclosure requirements, verify AI-generated outputs, and reconcile varying instructor expectations. However, explicit consideration of differences in technological access, language, accessibility, and institutional knowledge was less consistently evident across the reviewed documents. Drawing on hidden-curriculum and digital-inequality perspectives, the study identifies AI policy-navigation burdens and proposes the concept of a potential policy-navigation divide. While the findings do not establish unequal student experiences or educational outcomes, they highlight institutional conditions through which inequalities could emerge. The study recommends clearer policy communication, transparent assessment-specific expectations, accessible AI-literacy support, and greater attention to equity in institutional AI governance.

title: The emancipation of technology as a subject: teachers’ views of technology content in secondary education
abstractText: Abstract The roles of technology and engineering within STEM education have evolved from a focus on technology as a product to a broader vision encompassing the processes involved in its creation, closely linked to engineering. As the newest disciplines in STEM education, technology and engineering lack a well-defined identity, leading to uncertainty among educators about what and how to teach these subjects in K–12 education. This study proposes a comprehensive framework integrating multiple perspectives on essential knowledge in technology and engineering education, ranging from hands-on skills to theoretical, epistemological understanding, in order to characterize pre-service and in-service teachers’ perception about technology as a content for secondary education. Our findings reveal that teachers’ views represent a mosaic of complementary perspectives rather than a unified vision, reflecting ongoing identity challenges in these fields. Notably, both novice and experienced teachers display diverse conceptions, highlighting gaps potentially rooted in limited training and the shift from traditional technical to design-oriented learning outcomes. Additionally, teachers tend to emphasize practical knowledge over theoretical aspects and often perceive engineering design as a linear, procedural process rather than an epistemic activity. These limitations restrict the depth of student learning and hinder integration of core disciplinary knowledge. Importantly, some teachers incorporate perspectives on the nature of technology, enhancing the subject’s legitimacy. We argue for developing initial and continuous teacher training that fosters a rich, epistemologically informed vision of technology and engineering education consolidating these subjects as essential components of STEM education.

title: Estimating the Heritability of Intelligence with a Nuclear Twin Family Design
abstractText: Abstract Intelligence, and the favorable life outcomes with which it is associated, are not shared equally between individuals or groups. In an endeavor to better understand the inequality, behavioral genetics (BG) have employed the classical twin design (CTD) to apportion the variability in the intelligence quotient (IQ) to genetic and environmental sources. Recent research has revealed that such parameter estimates are subject to bias: underestimating the influence of assortative mating, and nonadditive genetic effects. These biases are somewhat mitigated by the nuclear twin family design (NTFD). To date no published studies have applied the NTFD to IQ. This study addresses this limitation utilizing a meta-analysis of data comprising IQ measures from 660,365 twin, parent-child, and spousal pairs collected over more than 50 years from more than 15 countries. In a comparison of parameter estimates obtained under the CTD and NTFD, this study confirmed that the NTFD more accurately estimated the heritability of IQ. These findings will inform and guide future research, gene-mapping efforts, and public policy aimed at correcting the inequality in educational and life outcomes that are significantly associated with IQ.

title: Different stimulation methods for the rat treadmill exercise model used in cardiovascular disease research
abstractText: Objective This paper aims to investigate the effectiveness of different stimulation methods on continuous treadmill exercise in rats, and to provide a rat treadmill exercise model used in cardiovascular disease research. Methods Experimental rats were divided into 3 exercise intensity groups: low-intensity(L-EX), moderate-intensity(M-EX), and high-intensity(H-EX). Different stimulation methods (tactile, auditory, light, and electrical) were used to intervene when rats stopped during treadmill training. The number of successful stimulations was counted, and electrocardiograms (ECG) of the exercise process were recorded. Results The success rate of both tactile stimulation and electrical stimulation was higher in the 3 different exercise intensity groups. The success rate of auditory stimulation was lower in the H-EX group than in the L-EX and M-EX groups. The success rate of light stimulation gradually decreased with the increase in exercise intensity. Overall, the other three stimulation methods were more successful than light stimulation. Furthermore, when electrical stimulation was used, ECG recordings showed marked baseline drift and waveform distortion caused by electrical artifacts, which made reliable interpretation of cardiac signals difficult. Conclusion In constructing a rat treadmill exercise model for cardiovascular disease research, tactile stimulation appears preferable among the tested methods when the rat stops on the treadmill, as it effectively motivates continued running without interfering with ECG recordings.

title: Unveiling the Chasm in Japanese robot-assisted surgery diffusion: the interplay of surgical volume and intra-specialty spillover
abstractText: Abstract To examine structural factors associated with the diffusion of robot-assisted surgery (RAS) in Japan, this study examined the associations of annual surgical volume, defined as the sum of open, conventional laparoscopic, and RAS cases, and prior intra-specialty experience with adoption speed. Using the 1st to 10th editions of the National Database of Health Insurance Claims and Specific Health Checkups of Japan (NDB) Open Data across fiscal years 2014–2023, diffusion trajectories were visualized for 21 procedures approved for insurance coverage by 2020 through bivariate plots of annual surgical volume versus RAS replacement rates. RAS diffusion exhibited non-linear dynamics associated with annual procedure volume. In niche markets with < 6,000 annual cases ( n = 9), six procedures demonstrated high growth in RAS replacement rate. Conversely, among 12 procedures with ≥ 6,000 annual cases, four did not cross the 16.0% chasm threshold through FY2023, and three required 6 years to surpass it. These patterns were thought to reflect challenges in the transition from specialized centers to general hospitals. Furthermore, a trend consistent with “intra-specialty spillover” was observed, wherein procedures approved in FY2020 achieved higher initial adoption than those in FY2018; although inseparable from the overall expansion of RAS since 2018, this suggests that accumulated infrastructure and expertise may facilitate the uptake of subsequent techniques. These findings suggest that RAS diffusion is associated with annual procedure volume, organizational readiness, and specialty‑specific infrastructure alongside technical factors. Future implementation strategies may benefit from infrastructure sharing within and across specialties and resource optimization to bridge the observed diffusion chasm.

title: Cost-driven design and optimization of steel support structures for offshore energy platforms: a review of CAPEX cost models
abstractText: Steel support structures for offshore energy platforms require large volumes of steel and complex manufacturing, making them one of the most expensive elements of any offshore project. Capital expenditure (CAPEX), which includes material procurement, manufacturing, transportation, and installation, typically makes up around 70% of the total lifecycle cost of these structures. Although many studies have proposed cost models to support design and optimization, the approaches used vary considerably in terms of scope, methodology, and level of detail. This paper reviews existing CAPEX cost models for fixed and floating steel offshore structures, covering jackets, monopiles, spar buoys, semi-submersibles, and tension leg platforms, based on peer-reviewed work published mainly between 2000 and 2026. Moreover, this study offers a new quantitative framework that combines cost model completeness, modelling detail, and structural complexity to compare studies. The findings show that material costs appear in 98% of studies, with 66.7% relying on material cost alone. Manufacturing costs have been included in 29% of studies, even though they can account for more than 30% of total production costs in welded steel structures. Transportation and installation costs have received less attention, appearing in 16% and 20% of studies, respectively. Only 14.1% of the reviewed studies include all four CAPEX components together. Finally, the key gaps identified across the reviewed literature are discussed, along with recommendations for future work.

Constraints on Compact Dark Matters Population from microlensing Effect of Gravitational Wave for the third-generation gravitational Wave Detector
abstractText: Abstract Since the first direct detection of gravitational waves (GWs) from a binary black-hole merger by the LIGO-Virgo Collaboration, GWs have emerged as a powerful probe of astrophysics and cosmology. If extragalactic compact dark matter (DM) candidates, such as primordial black holes, constitute a non-negligible fraction of the DM component over a broad mass range, they can imprint distinctive microlensing signatures on GW signals. In this work, we develop a framework to infer the population properties of extragalactic compact DM by simulating microlensing GWs in the frequency band of the third-generation ground-based GW detector, the Einstein Telescope, and analyzing them via hierarchical Bayesian inference. For a population described by a power-law mass function, we show that the detection of only several microlensing GW events among $10^4$ binary black-hole coalescences can constrain the compact DMs abundance to the level of $\sim 10^{-3}$. This forecast demonstrates that searching for and identifying microlensing signatures in future GW observations can provide a complementary approach to constraining compact DM scenarios.

title: Implementation of the Structured Debate Learning Model to Improve Learning Outcomes in Pancasila Education on the Topic of "the Territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia" at UPT SMP Negeri 3 Semanding
abstractText: Low initial learning mastery highlighted the need for more active instruction in Pancasila Education at UPT SMP Negeri 3 Semanding. This study examined changes in learning outcomes following the implementation of structured debate on the territory of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia (NKRI), with students divided into affirmative and opposing groups. A mixed-methods classroom action research design was conducted over two cycles involving 26 seventh-grade students in Class VII-C. Data were collected through observations, questionnaires/tests, and interviews and analyzed descriptively using quantitative and qualitative techniques. At baseline, two students (8%) met the minimum mastery criterion (KKM = 70), and the class mean score was 55. In Cycle I, mastery increased to 16 students (62%), with a mean score of 71. In Cycle II, mastery remained at 16 students (62%), while the mean score was 69. Qualitative findings indicated a progression from basic conceptual understanding toward analysis involving higher-order thinking skills, accompanied by greater self-confidence and stronger argumentation skills. These findings indicate that mastery gains relative to baseline were maintained across the two cycles, alongside qualitative improvements in students’ thinking and participation. The study provides contextual evidence for constructivist, debate-based civic pedagogy and practical insights for teachers seeking to strengthen analytical thinking, confidence, and argumentation through structured classroom debate.

title: Chronic disease count and fall-related characteristics among community-dwelling older adults: a cross-sectional study of recurrent falls and fall timing
abstractText: Background Chronic conditions and falls commonly co-occur in older populations. This study described fall occurrence, recurrent falls, and participant-level fall timing across chronic disease count groups in a single-city community sample. Methods This cross-sectional survey included 610 community-dwelling adults aged ≥60 years in Neijiang, Sichuan, China. Self-reported falls during the preceding 12 months were classified by occurrence and frequency; recurrent falls were defined as ≥2 falls. One participant-level fall-timing category was analyzed per faller. Chronic disease count was an unweighted sum of seven disease domains. Crude and minimally adjusted logistic regression described count associations. Disease-specific crude associations, post-LASSO models, and an equal-duration morning-versus-afternoon comparison were exploratory analyses. Results Overall, 303 participants (49.7%) reported falls and 96 (15.7%) reported recurrent falls. Fall occurrence was non-monotonic across count groups (52.9%, 42.2%, 47.8%, 56.6%, and 68.6% for 0, 1, 2, 3, and ≥4 diseases); corresponding recurrent-fall proportions were 9.6%, 12.9%, 16.5%, 19.7%, and 37.3%. The minimally adjusted OR for recurrent falls in the ≥4 group versus 0 was 4.85 (95% CI 2.06–11.46). The five-category timing distribution did not show clear evidence of an overall difference (Pearson p = 0.195). The morning/non-morning contrast had p = 0.024, and the equal-duration comparison included 203 fallers (108 morning and 95 afternoon; p = 0.011). Disease-specific estimates varied across diseases and outcomes. Post-LASSO findings remained exploratory. Conclusion Fall-related characteristics differed across chronic disease count groups in this Neijiang sample, particularly with respect to recurrent falls. Timing differences depended on the comparison used. These cross-sectional findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish temporal or causal relationships. Prospective, multicenter studies are required.

title: Long-term post-trial extension of osilodrostat therapy in selected Canadian patients with Cushing disease from the LINC 3 and LINC 4 programs
abstractText: Background Long-term outcomes of selected patients who continue osilodrostat for Cushing disease after clinical-trial participation remain incompletely described. Methods We retrospectively analyzed a selected multicenter post-trial cohort of Canadian patients with Cushing disease previously enrolled in LINC 3 (NCT02180217) or LINC 4 (NCT02697734) who continued osilodrostat in the global roll-over study and, when applicable, in a Canadian investigator-initiated extension phase (ISS-CA-2023; NCT06131580). The dataset included 11 Canadian osilodrostat-exposed LINC participants who entered post-trial roll-over follow-up; 7 subsequently entered the Canadian investigator-initiated extension, whereas 4 discontinued during earlier follow-up for defined reasons. For longitudinal efficacy analyses, baseline and time zero were defined as first osilodrostat exposure in the parent LINC study; week 14 refers to week 14 after osilodrostat initiation. The main outcomes were time to first mean urinary free cortisol (mUFC) control, durability of control, long-term dose evolution, pituitary tumor surveillance, and safety. Results Eleven selected Canadian patients received continued osilodrostat, and all achieved first biochemical control after a median of 5 weeks (range: 2–12). Median mUFC decreased from 2.65 × ULN at parent-study baseline to 0.56 × ULN at week 14; these descriptive values were not used for inferential testing. Seven patients remained on therapy long term; at the last follow-up, six of seven had controlled mUFC after a median exposure of 98 months (range: 83 to 121). Maintenance doses varied widely, with a median last-visit dose of 6 mg/day (range: 0.125 to 40), and several patients required progressive down-titration over time. Hypocortisolism/adrenal-insufficiency events were common and generally managed with dose interruption or reduction and temporary glucocorticoid replacement. Clinically significant pituitary tumor enlargement leading to discontinuation and surgery occurred in two patients. Conclusion In this selected Canadian post-trial continuation cohort, osilodrostat was associated with rapid initial biochemical control and durable long-term control in many patients for up to 10 years. The findings support the feasibility of long-term individualized osilodrostat management in selected patients continuing therapy after LINC 3/LINC 4 participation, with ongoing need for dose adaptation and surveillance for adrenal insufficiency and pituitary tumor behavior.

title: Exercise-induced hypoalgesia following HIIT: associations with cardiac interoceptive accuracy and the moderation by physical fitness
abstractText: Introduction Exercise-induced hypoalgesia (EIH) refers to the reduction in pain perception following acute exercise, yet the roles of aerobic fitness and interoception in this response remain unclear. Methods This study investigated pain perception and cardiac interoceptive accuracy before and after high-intensity interval training (HIIT) in endurance athletes and non-athletes. Forty-one healthy adults (20 athletes, 21 non-athletes) completed a maximal cardiopulmonary exercise test to determine VO₂max and self-report measures, including the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA). On a second study day, participants underwent pressure pain testing and a HBDT before and after HIIT. Training status was operationalized both categorically (athletes vs. non-athletes) and continuously (VO₂max). Results Athletes showed greater EIH than non-athletes, reflected in a significant reduction in pain following HIIT in athletes only and a larger pain change score compared with non-athletes. Higher VO₂max was likewise associated with greater pain reduction. Baseline cardiac interoceptive accuracy was positively associated with VO₂max, and interoceptive accuracy decreased significantly from pre- to post-exercise in both groups, with a more pronounced decline in athletes. MAIA scores showed no significant associations. VO₂max also significantly moderated the relation between post-exercise changes in cardiac interoceptive accuracy and pain reduction, suggesting that the link between interoceptive change and EIH differed as a function of aerobic fitness. Discussion From an adaptation-based, hormesis-informed perspective, the findings are compatible with a distinction between acute cost and longer-term adaptation: intense exercise may transiently reduce cardiac interoceptive accuracy, while repeated exposure may be associated with better baseline interoceptive accuracy and more effective post-exercise pain modulation.

title: Nonlinear relationship between serum LH levels on hCG trigger day and live birth rates in patients with fresh embryo transfer: a retrospective cohort study
abstractText: Background In assisted reproductive technology (ART), the assessment of sex hormones is indispensable. Maintaining an appropriate level of luteinizing hormone (LH) is crucial for ovarian and endometrial development. However, the relationship between LH concentrations on the hCG trigger day and pregnancy outcomes after fresh embryo transfer (ET) remains relatively unclear. The aim of our study was to explore the role of serum LH levels in live birth rates (LBRs) and its specific relationship. Methods We conducted a retrospective analysis of 9,044 patients who underwent fresh embryo transfer from 2019 to 2024. A multivariate regression model was used to identify the relationship. Stratification analysis was performed to test for effect modification in subgroups. The generalized additive model (GAM) and two-piecewise model were employed to describe the nonlinear relationship. Results We found a positive relationship between serum LH levels and LBRs when LH concentrations were lower than 4.31 mIU/ml (odds ratio [OR] = 1.06, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 1.00-1.12, P = 0.042). No significant relationship was observed when LH concentrations were higher than 4.31 mIU/ml. In the exploratory subgroup analyses, the similar association was identified in GnRH agonist cycles, with an inflection point at 4.09 mIU/mL. The significant interaction was also identified between infertility type and serum LH levels in relation to LBRs. Conclusions Our research found the nonlinear relationship between serum levels on the hCG trigger day and LBRs. We tentatively identified an inflection point at 4.31 mIU/ml, and further studies are warranted to validate its potential clinical utility.

Early-onset colorectal cancer burden in China from 1990 to 2023: a systematic analysis based on the Global Burden of Disease Study 2023
abstractText: Background Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) impairs the health of China’s working-age population and causes substantial socioeconomic costs. National long-term epidemiological data integrating trend segmentation, risk attribution and medium-term forecasting for domestic EOCRC remain insufficient. This study analysed China’s 33-year EOCRC burden (1990-2023), identified trend inflection points, quantified modifiable risk-attributable burden and predicted epidemic trends to support tiered prevention strategies. Methods Data on EOCRC burden among Chinese residents aged 15–49 were derived from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. We analyzed absolute cases and age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, DALYs and prevalence. Joinpoint regression detected segmented nonlinear trends, and Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models projected burden for 2024-2040. Dietary, metabolic and behavioural risk-attributable burden was quantified. Results From 1990 to 2023, national EOCRC mortality and DALY burden decreased continuously, whereas incident and prevalent cases increased significantly. Gender and age gradients existed: males and residents aged 45–49 carried the highest disease burden with slower improvement. Low milk and whole grain intake were the leading risk contributors, while high processed meat and high BMI showed rapidly rising attributable burden. All four burden indicators presented multi-stage trends and rebounded after 2020. ARIMA forecasts indicated age-standardized mortality and DALY rates would keep decreasing by 2040, yet male-dominated burden gaps remain prominent. Conclusion China’s EOCRC presents divergent long-term burden trends and stable age-sex disparities. The high burden in the 45–49 age group supports prioritizing this population for further screening evaluation, and male-oriented lifestyle interventions may help curb growing incidence and alleviate youth colorectal cancer burden.
